items.heading: These Numbers Come From Nasscom,
items.text: These numbers come from Nasscom, news reports of company filings, and industry reports. Read the meaning column, not only the figure.

items.heading: NASSCOM Splits the Sector Into
items.text: Nasscom splits the sector into five parts. Which part you enter shapes your pay ceiling, your daily work and how easily you can leave. The cards below lead with the parts that scale furthest, then the ones that need a plan.

visuals.heading: What the 2026 Numbers Actually Say

rows: USD 315 billion, up 6.1% (Nasscom Strategic Review, 24 February 2026).
The industry is still growing. The money is not the problem.
59.5 lakh people, up by about 1.35 lakh, which is 2.3% (Nasscom, same release).
Jobs grew at well under half the pace of revenue. More work is being done per person.
Five largest IT services firms, FY26
Combined headcount fell by 7,389 after a gain of 12,718 in FY25 (IANS, 25 April 2026). One other outlet counts 6,981, so the exact figure varies by source.
The big services names are no longer a guaranteed ramp for every graduate.
Fresher plans at the largest firms
TCS plans about 25,000 freshers in FY27, against 40,000 to 42,000 in earlier years. Infosys expects about 20,000 (IANS, 25 April 2026).
Seats exist, but fewer than the batch before you expected.
